title: Speeding Up OneDep Depositions of Multiple Related 3DEM Entries with pdb_extract
content: The Protein Data Bank (PDB) was established in 1971 as the first open-access digital resource in biology with just seven deposited protein structures. Today, the single global PDB archive houses more than 231,000 experimentally-determined three-dimensional (3D) structures of biological macromolecules, covering a vast array of molecular components and complexes in biological systems. These atomic-level structures have been meticulously curated by expert biocurators, who review all aspects of the submitted experimental data, including the key structural information, experimental conditions, data processing details, and validation statistics. This information is archived in the machine-parsable and extensible PDBx/mmCIF format and model quality is summarized in an official worldwide PDB (wwPDB) validation report [1]. Open access to PDB data without limitations on usage allows researchers from all over the world to explore 3D structures for insights into disease mechanisms, therapeutic targets, and molecular interactions. Unrestricted access has also played a critical role in the cryo-EM resolution revolution, as well as the development of AI/ML software tools such as AlphaFold, RosettaFold, and OpenFold. Today, more than one million public-domain computed structure models are being delivered alongside experimental structures by the Research Collaboratory for Structural Bioinformatics Protein Data Bank (RCSB PDB, RCSB.org) [2-3].
